headline: Brent crude drops 5% to $91 per barrel despite Middle East shipping risks
summary: Brent crude oil prices fell 5% to $91 per barrel this week as recovering crude flows from the Middle East Gulf to Asian buyers offset tanker attacks and escalating regional tensions.
why: Brent crude is the primary international benchmark for oil pricing, directly affecting global energy costs, transportation rates, and inflation.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: Ample Middle Eastern physical crude deliveries satisfied Asian demand, pulling benchmark futures lower.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Strong physical shipments from Middle Eastern producers alleviated market fears of immediate global supply disruption.
